title: Empire Biscuits
subtitle: Scottish iced shortbread sandwiched with jam
excerpt: Two rounds of crisp shortbread sandwiched with raspberry jam, topped with white glacé icing, and finished with a single glacé cherry. A beloved Scottish teatime biscuit.

recipe.sourceNotes: Empire biscuits are a fixture of Scottish bakeries, church sales, and school fetes. They are known by various names: 'Imperial biscuits' in some parts of Scotland, 'doubles' elsewhere, 'German biscuits' in their original form before anti-German sentiment during World War One prompted the name change to 'empire'. The biscuit is essentially a sandwich biscuit: two plain shortbread rounds joined with jam, glazed with white icing, and decorated with a glacé cherry. The shortbread should be very pale, barely coloured at the edges. The icing should be thick enough to set firmly but not so thick that it is difficult to eat. Homemade versions are always better than bought ones because the icing is applied to the biscuit while slightly warm, and the jam is plentiful.

content.text: The shortbread must be crisp, not soft: it needs to hold the weight of the jam and icing without going soggy. Roll it to an even 5 mm thick and do not overbake. The biscuits should be pale golden, not brown. Let them cool completely before sandwiching with jam. Apply the icing while the biscuits are slightly warm but not hot: this gives a neater set. Use a generous amount of jam.
Heat the oven to 180 C / fan 160 C / gas 4. Beat the butter and sugar until just combined, not fluffy. Add the vanilla and salt. Stir in the flour until a soft dough forms.

Roll out on a lightly floured surface to 5 mm thick. Cut into rounds using a 6 cm cutter. Re-roll the trimmings. Place on lined baking trays and bake for 10 to 12 minutes until pale golden at the edges. Cool for 5 minutes on the tray, then transfer to a rack.
When cool, spread half the biscuits with a generous layer of raspberry jam. Sandwich with the remaining biscuits.

Sift the icing sugar into a bowl and mix in enough cold water, a teaspoon at a time, to form a thick, spreadable icing. Spread over the top of each sandwiched biscuit and immediately press half a glacé cherry into the centre. Leave to set for 30 minutes before serving.
